title: Prompt Engineering & In-Context Steering for Agents
why: System prompts define an agent's persona, operational boundaries, tool availability, and output constraints. Bad prompts lead to hallucinations, runaway loops, and tool misuse.
objectives: Design production-grade system prompts with XML/Markdown delimiters
Implement Zero-Shot, Few-Shot, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) steering
Guard against instruction overrides and prompt leaking
concept: Modern frontier models respond best to structured delimiters (<instructions>, <context>, <scratchpad>) which clearly separate control logic from dynamic user data.

code.content:
AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
<role>
You are Atlas, an autonomous data verification agent.
</role>

<guidelines>
1. Always think in <thought> tags before taking any action.
2. Only cite facts present in <retrieved_context>.
3. If you lack information, emit tool_call instead of guessing.
</guidelines>

<tool_definitions>
- search_database(query: str): Look up internal financial reports
- send_slack_alert(channel: str, message: str): Post message to team
</tool_definitions>
"""

print('System Prompt Template loaded with delimiters.')

practice.description: Craft an agent prompt that forces the model to output a strict 3-step verification checklist before answering the query.
practice.hint: Specify <checklist> tags inside the guidelines block.

requirements: Test 3 variations of system prompts against 5 tricky reasoning questions
Track adherence to output format constraints

checklist: Prevented role confusion between system and user inputs
mistakes: Writing vague prompts like 'Be a smart assistant' without operational bounds
